key_insight: LLM-generated note bloat modestly reduced downstream summary quality, while diagnostic overcalls propagated into later LLM outputs without detectable changes in standard quality metrics.
clinical_relevance: AI-assisted documentation can influence later AI-generated summaries, making the origin and certainty of recorded information important to track.
method: Evaluated seven reader models from four model families on downstream hospital-course generation.
Compared accumulated LLM summaries with copy-forward and templated text of matched length.
Injected unconfirmed differential diagnoses and tested whether reader models repeated them.
evidence_signal: Across the tested models, LLM summaries modestly but consistently degraded downstream generation, and overcall repetition varied by reader model.
watch_item: Standard quality metrics may miss propagated diagnostic overcalls; the abstract does not establish effects on patient outcomes.
paper_title: AI in the Clinical Documentation Loop: Effects of LLM-Induced Note Bloat and Diagnostic Overcall on Downstream LLMs
